evidence.locator: Department of Justice introduction; central-assistance guidelines dated16December2009paragraph2
evidence.qualification: Do not confuse the short-title year2008 with Act4of2009 or commencement. No current court count is inferred.

evidence.target: Nyayadhikari appointment and first-class judicial-magistrate eligibility
evidence.qualification: State Government consults High Court. This is a judicial office, not election of a village functionary. Section6 states eligibility, not that every appointee must already hold a particular current magistrate posting.

evidence.target: Mobile proceedings plus statutorily limited civil and criminal jurisdiction
evidence.qualification: Mobility does not create unlimited jurisdiction. Section9 also requires publicity when sitting outside headquarters. The printed two-year/20000-rupee blanket claim is not adopted.

evidence.target: Separate criminal and civil appeal forums
evidence.qualification: Permitted criminal appeals go to Court of Session; permitted civil appeals to District Court. The answer is expressly subject to statutory exclusions. A blanket source statement sending every appeal to Sessions is defective.

evidence.target: Family Court establishment after consultation and population exceeding one million
evidence.qualification: Exceeding one million is not the same as exactly one million. Establishment after consultation is distinct from section4appointment with High Court concurrence.

evidence.target: Qualified duty to endeavour towards settlement
evidence.qualification: First-instance endeavour operates where possible consistently with the case’s nature and circumstances. It is not compulsory settlement or a bar to adjudication.

evidence.target: No legal-practitioner representation entitlement as of right
evidence.qualification: The amicus-curiae proviso permits legal-expert assistance in the interests of justice. No absolute ban on all legal assistance is taught.

evidence.target: Qualified High Court appeal on facts and law
evidence.qualification: Interlocutory orders and consent decrees/orders are excluded from the general route; maintenance orders receive separate statutory treatment. The prepared reader’s single-appeal summary is not accepted without these qualifications. No contested appeal-limitation rule is tested.
